uutiset.t: Dubai Said to Eye Consolidating Lenders in Islamic Banking Push
uutiset.s: Officials in Dubai have held preliminary talks on potentially combining Dubai Islamic Bank with Emirates Islamic Bank to create a Sharia-compliant lender better positioned to compete globally, people familiar with the matter said.

uutiset.t: India’s Banking Cash Turns to Deficit for First Time Since June
uutiset.s: India’s banking system liquidity slipped into deficit for the first time in about five months, as tax outflows left banks strapped for cash.

uutiset.t: India’s New Data Series to Aid RBI Policy, Gupta Says
uutiset.s: India’s new economic data series will help the Reserve Bank of India make more accurate forecasts of growth and inflation and better calibrate monetary policy, Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta said Monday.

uutiset.t: Capita Dives 66% as CEO Quits Over Botched Pensions Contract
uutiset.s: Capita Plc shares plummeted by nearly two-thirds after its chief executive officer stepped down over failings in the outsourcing company’s contract managing Britain’s Civil Service pensions.

uutiset.t: Vitol Unit Sets Timeline for $2.3 Billion Durban LNG Power Plant
uutiset.s: Vitol Group’s Engen Petroleum plans to start building a 40 billion rand ($2.3 billion) power plant in the eastern South African city of Durban that will run on liquefied natural gas in about two years, a project that could help grow local demand for the fuel.

uutiset.t: Coca-Cola HBC Rises in JSE Debut Ahead of $2.6 Billion Deal
uutiset.s: Coca-Cola HBC AG rose in its Johannesburg trading debut, adding one of the world’s biggest bottlers of the beverage to Africa’s largest stock exchange days before it completes a $2.6 billion acquisition that will significantly expand its presence on the continent.

uutiset.t: Malaysia Palm Industry Says CPO Tax-Waiver Window Has Passed
uutiset.s: Malaysia’s palm oil industry says the window in which an export tax waiver would have helped boost shipments and ease a buildup in stockpiles has passed.

uutiset.t: S. Korea’s Market Measures Fall Short of Stemming Stock Selloff
uutiset.s: South Korea reiterated its commitment to stabilize equity markets, but the measures failed to soothe investor sentiment, with the benchmark Kospi ending lower Monday following last week’s selloff.

uutiset.t: European Gas Surges as Cold Snap Threatens Tight Inventories
uutiset.s: European natural gas prices jumped after temperature forecasts shifted sharply lower, adding pressure on inventories already strained by export disruptions stemming from the US-Iran war.

uutiset.t: MSCI Aired Avoiding Indonesia Downgrade With Prabowo, Dalio
uutiset.s: MSCI Inc. Chief Executive Henry Fernandez conveyed a willingness to consider alternatives to a two-step downgrade of Indonesia’s stock-market status in recent direct talks with President Prabowo Subianto, according to people with knowledge of the discussion.
